nodes.label: Skill File Schema — Frontmatter + Body Pattern
nodes.rationale: Every shipped skill follows YAML frontmatter (name, description, version, trigger[], integrations[], inputs[], output_artifact, frequency, pack) and five H2 body sections (When to run, What you'll get, Steps, Output format, Example output). Vault overrides win on name conflict, preventing git pull from clobbering user edits.
nodes.norm_label: skill file schema — frontmatter + body pattern

nodes.label: FreeLLM Proxy — 16+ Provider Router
nodes.rationale: Express 5 + TypeScript ESM monorepo; acts as the single OpenAI-compatible endpoint that all LLM traffic funnels through; supports streaming, tool calling, embeddings with family-based routing, encrypted key storage via AES-256-GCM, rate-limit failover, health checks, and a React/Vite admin dashboard.

nodes.label: Hybrid RAG — BM25 + Embedding Fusion
nodes.rationale: Combines BM25 lexical retrieval with dense MiniLM embeddings fused via Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF); serves as the knowledge base grounding all debate turns; backed by SQLite FTS5 + FAISS vector store.

nodes.label: Debate Engine — Character Roleplay Loop
nodes.rationale: Python/FastAPI server (:5050) running character-driven adversarial roleplay; uses LangChain ChatOpenAI for turn generation; 38 persona cards from SillyTavern; debates produce a transcript fed to the Judge for spec distillation.

nodes.label: Agent Dispatcher — Headless CLI Execution
nodes.rationale: Server on :5090 providing judge→task-spec→CLI dispatch; roles gate tool access (code_task only to Engineers/Operator); results reviewed by team panel (Reviewer+Judge+Engineer+Security) who vote APPROVE/REJECT; rejected work loops back with feedback up to dispatch_max_retries.

nodes.label: Telegram Bridge — Remote Team Access
nodes.rationale: Long-polling bot relay (@kaggle_shot_bot) connecting Telegram group chats to the Business surface; slash commands (/team, /topic, /ask, /speak, /judge, /status, /reset) mirror the web UI operations.

nodes.label: Prompt Defense Baseline — Universal Security Policy
nodes.rationale: Every persona file includes an identical Prompt Defense Baseline section forbidding role changes, secret leakage, unvalidated executable output, unicode/homoglyph tricks, token overflow manipulation, urgency/emotional pressure tactics, authority claims, and harmful content generation. This is an architectural guardrail applied uniformly across all 10 personas.
nodes.norm_label: prompt defense baseline — universal security policy

nodes.label: code_task Grant — Executor-Level Permission Gate
nodes.rationale: code_task is an explicit tool grant assigned to Kai (Builder), June (Inspector), Ona (Operator), and Sam (Reviewer). It dispatches headless claude/opencode agents but is purpose-limited: Kai writes product code; June/Sam run verification only; Ona handles infra work only. This enforces hard permission boundaries at the executor level rather than relying on prompt suggestions.

nodes.label: Next.js 15 App Router Console
nodes.rationale: React + TypeScript + Tailwind with shadcn-style local components; serves the Business surface at :18443; talks to Hermes api_server on port 8642; all /api/* routes gated by validateToken(); uses ephemeral localhost-bound session tokens written to ~/.hermes/agentic-os/token.

nodes.label: Vault Zone Access Model — sources/wiki/journal/schema
nodes.rationale: Four-zone ownership model enforced by lib/vault.ts: sources/ (read-only agent), wiki/ (read+write agent, draft→reviewed→stable lifecycle), journal/ (user-write only), schema/ (read-only). Agents cannot modify reviewed/stable pages without explicit instruction. This prevents silent corruption of curated knowledge.

nodes.label: LangChain Integration in Debate Service
nodes.rationale: services/debate/ uses ChatOpenAI for character turns, HuggingFace embeddings, FAISS vectorstore, and text splitters. Explicitly NOT using LangGraph or LangSmith despite LangChain being installed as a transitive dependency.

nodes.label: SQLite Storage Layer
nodes.rationale: Used by FreeLLM proxy for encrypted key storage (better-sqlite3 + AES-256-GCM), by Hermes for state.db, by Console for vault.db (FTS5 + vector index built by scripts/index_vault.py). All three use SQLite but for different purposes with different schemas.

nodes.label: Agent-to-Agent Protocol (A2A)
nodes.rationale: The debate→judge→dispatch pipeline implements an implicit A2A pattern: characters (agents) debate with tool access, the judge aggregates their outputs into a structured task spec, and dispatch agents execute subtasks headlessly. This mirrors the A2A spec's division between agent card/profile and task execution.
